page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the average tier for general compute tasks, with a Passmark CPU score of 34,961.9 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 12,846.0. The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. In memory bandwidth tests, it achieves 126.91 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 58.65 GB/sec for writes. Notably, the instance demonstrates strong performance in lightweight LLM text generation, processing 266.46 tokens per second with a 135M parameter model, while maintaining average performance for larger 7B parameter models.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.c7.8xlarge offers a resource-dense profile tailored for compute-heavy workloads rather than memory-intensive databases. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable execution times, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for sustained processing tasks. Tradeoffs include the complete absence of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators, which limits its utility for heavy deep learning training or high-I/O local database operations. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and moderate-scale machine learning inference.
